videos.title: Building a Custom Pedalino Mini 6 MIDI Controller
videos.author: reshra
videos.description:
If you’re into DIY electronics definitely give this a go! USB midi pedals can be used for more than just music, for example triggering OBS scene changes or other shortcuts or macros on your computer.

Find the links to all the parts I used and other useful stuff on:
https://reshra.xyz

This was the first time I used 3D printed parts and it’s been a lot of fun building something genuinely useful. Follow along for the next parts in which I talk about and show the wiring and how I use this when playing guitar! 

By “respecting the wiring of a TRS port” I mean that if you were to connect a TRS port or cable to the micro controller you would need three pins: one for the tip, one for the ring, one for the sleeve (ground). On these pins you can technically send information from 1 momentary footswitch (one of the pins essentially being unused since you only need one), 2 footswitches, an expression pedal or other devices that use a TRS cable. So the “pedals” in the Pedalino software can support all of these because they are meant to represent a TRS connection.
If you want to use just one momentary footswitch you can, you just won’t use one of the pins and assign only one control for that pedal. Not the clearest abstraction but I managed to make sense of it now.

The tips shared in the last part should work on any midi pedal, the difference will just be how you set it up to send the different midi messages or sequences. 

I’m still experimenting with using it with the HX Stomp but the three scenarios I showed cover all of my use cases at the moment. As mentioned, I mostly stay on one preset and use snapshots to instantly change between different gain settings and can then use the free footswitches to toggle effects of parameter values. With 6 extra switches you really can control a lot more.

Perhaps a more advanced use case would be to have a different midi bank per HX Stomp preset or keep the same midi bank but be able to switch HX stomp presets. 

Another option I’ve seen is to not even use snapshots but just send multiple midi messages to achieve the same effect and toggle multiple footswitches or change multiple parameters at the same time. I believe there is a limit on how many messages you can send at the same time but if you don’t need that many then this would allow you to create more than three “snapshots”.

Imagination is your limit here but it depends a lot on what you want or need to do.

I didn’t touch on syncing the display and led state because the way I did it is very particular to Pedalino plus I added some custom code to make it work the way it does today.

Any questions or thoughts please drop them in the comments and we can talk!

videos.title: I Turned My Vox AC15 Into a Free Digital Amp (Part 1)
videos.author: reshra
videos.description:
Follow me as I show the process of creating a NAM A2 capture for my Vox AC15 tube amp. You can find all the links mentioned on my website below, including my amp capture.

https://reshra.xyz

In the next video I’ll show how to use this model in the DAW for recording and compare the output of that to the real amp recording.

I wanted to learn how to do this and decided to document the process, hopefully this helps someone else as well. Let me know if there are any questions!

On the DI point - you can skip the first step and jump straight to reamping the sweep signal without the “calibration” but it might just take a bit more trial and error.

What’s even cooler is you can use this same process to capture other analog gear such as pedals, you just send the pedal output directly into the interface rather than using a mic.

There are already pedals that have announced support for this technology so soon we’ll be able to use it live as well.

Btw, I post these on my TikTok first so follow me there to see them as soon as they come out:
https://www.tiktok.com/@reshra

videos.title: Can You Hear the Difference? Real Vox AC15 vs NAM Capture (Part 2)
videos.author: reshra
videos.description:
Did you get it right? 👀 Let me know in the comments

You can find all the links mentioned on my website below, including my amp capture shown in the video.

https://reshra.xyz

In this video I compare the real amp recording with the NAM capture and then show how you can load this capture into your DAW for recording. I'm still learning about this myself so please let me know if there's anything to improve!

I tried to get the recordings as close as possible in terms of LUFS but, like I said, I think I could tweak it even more to get it closer.

I’ve already seen posts about better VSTs so will have to play around with those and share an update. Please let me know if you’re already using one of these! 

I would also recommend Tudor's video and channel for a more detailed deep dive on the calibrated input part and how to use it:
